about: PROPOSED, UNSIGNED. One Proofline task, XC-55, part of the 'cover ALL' decomposition (XC-54 to XC-78) drafted on 2026-10-25 from public sources. Nothing here is binding and vv does not read this file. It becomes part of the contract only when the owner merges it into proofline.json and re-signs it with the owner key pinned in guard/owner.pub. Every criterion except scope, pushed and the unchanged-suite guards fails on the v1.6.0 tree. Evidence is testnet-only, loopback-only and verify-only unless the task says otherwise; hosted facilitators are never called. Estimated effort: 2-3 days.

not_contract_tasks.keys: Throwaway testnet keys and faucet tokens are created on the owner's machine and live in X402C_KEYS outside the repository. No spend, no mainnet.
not_contract_tasks.disclosure: A failing third-party column is reported to that project privately first (SECURITY.md). Until the window clears its row says 'under disclosure' with no per-check detail.

tasks.title: Spec-clause anchors pinned to upstream commits, a spec-drift report, and a crosswalk to the USENIX 2026 facilitator rules
tasks.description: Extends the XC-53 registry: each check id carries {spec_file, upstream_commit, line_start, line_end, quoted_text_sha256, profile}. tools/spec_anchors.py --check verifies offline against vendored spec snapshots under docs/spec-snapshots/<commit>/; --drift <commit> lists check ids whose anchored text changed (the property the #2776 review and #3396 asked for: a pinned spec version and an exact requirement reference per vector, and a separate optional security profile). docs/crosswalk/usenix-2026.json maps check ids to SR1-SR8 and Server-SR1-SR2 from Wang et al., USENIX Security 2026, citing the paper's public text only.

criteria.statement: Every normative check id names an upstream spec file, a pinned x402-foundation/x402 commit and a line anchor whose quoted text matches the file at that commit
Given a newer upstream spec commit, the drift report lists exactly the check ids whose anchored text changed
Every facilitator check maps to zero or more USENIX Security 2026 rules SR1-SR8 / Server-SR1-SR2, and each of SR1-SR8 is either mapped to a check id or listed as a gap with a task id
Security-profile and resilience checks are never labelled normative in docs/check-ids.json

verifier.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('docs/check-ids.json'));bad=[c['id'] for c in d['checks'] if c['profile']=='normative' and not c.get('anchor')];print(bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

criteria.statement: CI checks the anchors offline on every push
Every changed file is inside this task's scope

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.

Testnet only: never use a mainnet CAIP-2 id, never fund a key with anything but testnet faucet tokens, never call a hosted facilitator; every facilitator under test is the owner's own instance on 127.0.0.1.
A failing third-party result is not published with per-check detail until SECURITY.md's disclosure window clears; if a criterion would need that detail to pass, STOP and report.
